name: 197 · S Night Paparazzi G7X
description: Relight this image. Change nothing else: keep the existing background, setting and framing exactly as they are, add nothing to the scene, and keep the subject identity, pose, expression, hairstyle and clothing exactly as they are. A single hard flash sits on the lens axis and fires straight at the subject, lighting the front of the body flat and evenly with almost no modelling across the face, and throwing a hard-edged shadow onto the nearest surface behind them. THE FLASH MUST WIN ON THE SUBJECT: expose them about one and a half stops brighter than the room and hold their skin at a neutral 5500K, so it reads brighter, cleaner and cooler than everything around it and never takes on the room colour. This rule ensures all images have the distinct direct-flash, high-saturation, cool-foreground-warm-background aesthetic seen in these references. (Canon G7X III direct on-camera flash photography. High-contrast, sharp, and glossy finish. The subject is intensely illuminated by a cooler, daylight-balanced direct flash, creating bright specular highlights with rapidly falling-off light. A sharp, soft edge, dark drop shadow is cast immediately behind the subject,just like in each image in this collage,against the background. Contrast this by making the background elements (like walls, steps, and shelves) emit a very rich overly exaggerated warm, golden (2700K–3200K) tungsten-toned ambient light from integrated architectural sources. This background ambient light should be lower in relative intensity but create a soft, inviting, warm diffused glow, setting a dramatic and luxurious "night out" tone.) Push the speculars on skin hard: bright, exaggerated wet-looking sheen on forehead, cheekbones, nose bridge, collarbones, shoulders and arms, clipping toward white where the flash lands most directly, pores still visible so skin reads glossy and lit, not retouched. If eyes are visible, render catchlights as small bright round points from the on-axis flash, matched in both eyes.
